title: Local exclusion and regional decline of an endemic Galápagos tree species (Psidium galapageium Hook.) by an invasive relative (P. guajava L.)
content:
Abstract
Invasive species can interact with native relatives in a variety of ways that may jeopardize their long-term coexistence. Here we use a combination of species distribution modelling, geospatial analyses, in situ surveys of demography, and comparisons of fitness in sympatry and allopatry to investigate whether interactions with an invasive species of guava (Psidium guajava L.) may be contributing to the exclusion of guayabillo (P. galapageium Hook.), a tree species endemic to the Galápagos archipelago. We find evidence consistent with ongoing regional decline of guayabillo across the archipelago, with the extent of exclusion on each island coinciding with the date that guava was introduced. We rank extant guayabillo populations based on guava density in surrounding regions to identify high-priority management targets for guava removal.
